title: Regional Buffer Index — weekly snapshot and actions
content:
Purpose:
Quick weekly capture of the new Regional Buffer Index (RBI) signals, observations from the last 7 days, and a short action list for capacity/ops. This doc is intended as a working snapshot for the capacity sync and oncall handoff.

Executive summary:
- RBI v0.3 smoothing (6h exponential) rolled to production on 2028-01-05. Early read: improved false positive priming by ~22% (fewer unnecessary prewarm starts) while preserving overall headroom for bursts.
- US-WEST and EU-WEST holding near targets; APAC (asia-east1) dipped under target twice (Jan 6 & Jan 9) during short marketing-driven bursts. No customer-facing SLO misses but small latency bumps (~15–35ms p50 token).
- Short-term operational ask: add a transient 10% burst window to asia-east1 prewarm policy and run a 48h priming experiment with lower-start thresholds. Cost impact estimated +0.7% on weekly GPU-hours if accepted.

RBI definition / how to interpret numbers (brief):
- Buffer index = available prewarmed capacity as percent of expected 99th-percentile demand over next 30m, with 6h smoothing applied.
- Target buffer by region is currently: US-WEST 18%, US-EAST 12%, EU-WEST 15%, APAC 20% (APAC higher due to higher preemption risk and observed tail spikes).
- Emergency reserve = 5% global fallback (always kept for critical customers).

Snapshot (2028-01-03 to 2028-01-09) -- key rows: region | target | current median | min observed | notes
- us-west1 | 18% | 21% | 16% | healthy, priming latency stable, minor autoscaler oscillation Jan 7 03:20 UTC (investigated).
- us-east4 | 12% | 13% | 11% | smooth; small increase in background training batch jobs impacted ephemeral quota Jan 8 14:00 UTC (ticket INFRA-3721).
- europe-west1 | 15% | 16% | 14% | warm pool sizing appears right; traced a slow-deallocation bug in node-evict controller (PR in flight).
- asia-east1 | 20% | 9% | 6% | under target during two bursts tied to partner campaign; prewarm cold starts observed, p95 latency increased ~120ms during windows.

Observations and signal analysis:
- Smoothing tradeoff: v0.3 (6h tau) reduced flapping in regions with noisy short bursts (us-west1), but in APAC the smoothing made RBI slow to react to rapid short campaigns. We need asymmetric smoothing or a dual-horizon signal (30m fast lane + 6h slow lane).
- Correlated signals: marketing campaign metadata (tracked in the routing tag) correlates strongly with short APAC spikes. We can short-circuit RBI for tagged traffic and prewarm proactively when the campaign window is known.
- Cost vs risk: current policy keeps APAC buffer high; removing 5% would save ~1.8% weekly GPU cost in APAC but increases cold start probability by ~2.4% for the observed workload. Recommend cautious experiments rather than blanket change.

Incidents and triage notes (last 7d):
- Jan 6 11:12 UTC: APAC cold starts during partner campaign. Triggered auto-fallback to model-variant-s (smaller but slower quality). No data leak. Incident severity P2. Owner: Sofia Martins. Follow-up: implement campaign-tagged prewarm (INFRA-3810).
- Jan 7 03:18 UTC: Autoscaler oscillation, caused by background job bursts overlapping scaling cooldown. Root cause: cooldown window set to 60s; noisy telemetry gave repeated scale-up then down. Temporary mitigation: extend cooldown to 180s for small scale operations. Owner: Liam O'Rourke.

Experiment plan (short):
- APAC dual-horizon RBI experiment (48h)
  - Goal: keep long-term smoothing for stability but allow a fast 30m reactive lane for campaign-detected traffic.
  - Variant A: fast lane uses simple moving-average + signal gating on campaign tags.
  - Variant B: fast lane uses predictive model (short-term AR) seeded by campaign schedule.
  - Measurement: cold-start rate, p95 token latency, GPU-hours delta.
  - Owner: Maya Chen. Start: 2028-01-12, end: 2028-01-14.

Action items (owner / due):
- Maya: deploy dual-horizon config to asia-east1 canary (2028-01-12).
- Liam: extend scale cooldown for small autoscale groups and monitor oscillation metrics (2028-01-11).
- Sofia: add partner-campaign tag ingestion to the capacity pipeline (INFRA-3810) and produce a FAQ for oncall (2028-01-13).
- Arjun: run cost projection for the APAC 48h experiment and commit to rollback thresholds (2028-01-11).
- Noah: capture priming histogram snapshots every 10m during experiment and push to ephemeral S3 bucket for quick analysis (2028-01-12).

Runbook/ops notes for oncall:
- If RBI falls below 4% in any region and p95 token latency > 500ms -> escalate to infra-lead and enable emergency regional fallback (policy id: RB-FALLBACK-5).
- For campaign traffic spikes: check Campaign Tracker link (Slack: #growth-campaigns) and if scheduled, flip campaign prewarm gate to ON for affected region (manual override in console -> Capacity -> Region -> Campaign prewarm).

Questions / open issues:
- Should RBI expose a public metric per-customer tier so Sales can request ad-hoc buffer increases? (pros: transparency, cons: SLA complexity)
- Do we want to keep APAC target at 20% long-term, or use dynamic per-customer risk scores to drive targets?

Appendix: quick engineering notes
- RBI v0.3 release notes: smoothing=6h, emergency reserve enforced at allocation stage, gating by prewarm-tag added.
- Telemetry: added rbi_fast_lane.* counters and campaign-tag.* labels; dashboards updated (sheet id: dashboard/infra/rbi-v03).
- Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789 (dual-horizon scaffolding), github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/202 (cooldown changes).

Meeting cadence and invites:
- Weekly capacity sync: Tue 11:00 UTC (capacity, serving, SRE, product).
- RBI experiment standups: daily 09:30 UTC until experiment end (Maya).

Notes-to-self (rough):
- If fast lane yields too many false positives, add a lightweight classifier that uses campaign-engagement signal + recent-traffic slope to gate starts.
- Track cost delta at region level per 24h bin (not weekly) while experiments run.

Next snapshot planned: 2028-01-17 (post-APAC experiment).

End of note.
